mechanisms.decisive_claim: For fixed prime b and integer A>=4, the interval (X,2X), X=b^(floor(K/2)-A), contains enough primes for a path with s=floor(K/4), and balanced b-adic padding places its support-minimal unequal relation entirely in (N/b^6,N] while avoiding every prime below X.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use prime interval abundance, exact rough-part height, five-unit balancing, and path-kernel minimality for all sufficiently large K.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Repeated Bertrand postulate alone proves that one fixed interval (X,2X) contains at least K/2 primes for all sufficiently large exponential X.
mechanisms.kill_test: Inspect the logical content of Bertrand, which guarantees existence of one prime but no linear-in-K count in the same interval.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The same worst-case proof gives the tail (N/b^6,N] for A=3.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compare the guaranteed reserve 2A-2=4 with the possible five-unit decrement.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: For A>=4, evenly distributing the shore discrepancy always uses at most five exponent decrements per left vertex and leaves all padded exponents nonnegative.
mechanisms.kill_test: Write K=4s+r, bound Delta<5s+r, and subtract five from the reserve 2A-2.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The same degree-two path host works with every edge prime strictly greater than sqrt(N).
mechanisms.kill_test: Multiply the two incident edge primes at an internal vertex before padding.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Connectedness of the edge-prime path is unnecessary for support minimality.
mechanisms.kill_test: Disconnect the incidence graph and use one component to form a proper signed subrelation whenever its shore imbalance is nonzero.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The square-root-scale path lifts the deterministic zero-transcript dichotomy and the shared-seed bound Pr(transversal)<=E|D|/(L-t) for uniform adaptive valuation-query trees whose zero branch queries primes below X.
mechanisms.kill_test: Condition seedwise, construct a relation in every retain-labelled zero transcript, and charge at least L-t deletions on every successful seed.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every prime appearing anywhere in the decision tree must be below X for the zero-transcript obstruction to apply.
mechanisms.kill_test: Put an arbitrarily large prime only on a nonzero branch and verify that zero-transcript inputs never query it.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Expected o(N) deletion implies o(1) success even when the essential zero-transcript population L is o(N).
mechanisms.kill_test: Compare the exact ratio E|D|/(L-t) when E|D| is asymptotically larger than L.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The square-root query theorem also rules out a global repair phase of expected o(N) size.
mechanisms.kill_test: Repair the one seedwise missed path by deleting one selected vertex.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Conditioning on private per-input coins yields one uniform deterministic tree covered by the shared-seed theorem.
mechanisms.kill_test: Check that the conditioned programs remain indexed by the input integer and have no common zero transcript.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A finite verification of many primes in several intervals is sufficient to promote the all-parameter square-root-scale theorem.
mechanisms.kill_test: Remove the prime number theorem dependency and test whether finite intervals imply the claim for every sufficiently large K.
